en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government, composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives, is responsible for creating and passing laws.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Philippines over 2,000 years ago using traditional engineering.
General Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Sampaguita, scientifically known as Jasminum sambac, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934 because of its sweet fragrance.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a makeshift bamboo incubator for rural babies.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a rhythmic dance step that mimics the flowing current of the river.
Intramuros is the historic walled city within modern Manila that served as the seat of the Spanish colonial government for over three centuries.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, all citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right and duty to vote in elections.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippine government, while over one hundred twenty regional languages are spoken nationwide.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan and the Oblation to symbolize Filipino heroism and selfless offering.
